title: Faith and reason, 1870
hookLine: God can be known by reason from created things

cards: Why is there something rather than nothing? The philosopher Leibniz asked it that way, but children ask it without the polish, sometimes at bedtime. Why is there a world?
Who made the first thing? A tired parent might say, go to sleep. The First Vatican Council decided the question deserved a straight answer about what a human mind can and cannot reach on its own.
Today's word is Dei Filius, Vatican One's document on faith and reason.

teach.b: The council made three claims, and they fit together. First, reason can reach God.
Dei Filius teaches that God, the beginning and end of all things, can be known with certainty by the natural light of human reason, from the things he made.
It takes that straight from Saint Paul, in the Douay-Rheims: "For the invisible things of him, from the creation of the world, are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made."
You don't need a Bible to wonder where the world came from, and the council says the wondering can actually get somewhere.
Second, reason is not the whole road. God also revealed himself, so that the truths about him that reason could reach might be known by everyone, easily, firmly and without error mixed in.
And there are mysteries hidden in God, the council says, that reason could never find alone; Catholics name the Trinity as one.
Third, the two cannot truly fight.
In its fourth chapter the council says there can never be a real disagreement between faith and reason, because the same God who reveals the mysteries gave the mind its light.
If they seem to clash, either the faith has been misunderstood or an opinion has been mistaken for reason.
Faith should help reason, and reason should help faith. So the council refused to say the mind is useless in religion, and refused to say the mind is enough.

how: Catholic teaching holds that God can be known by reason from the created world and also through revelation, and Catholic schools and universities teach philosophy alongside theology on that basis.

games.q: a child asks at bedtime why there's a world at all. by Dei Filius's lights, what's that question?
o: a silly question with no answer.
a real road the mind can travel toward God.
a question only scripture may answer.
games.why: Vatican I taught that reason, starting from created things, can come to know God with certainty, while revelation shows more.

practice: Pick one thing within reach, a cup, your own hand, the floor, and ask of it slowly: why is this here, and why is there anything to be here at all?
Don't hurry to an answer; let the question stay open and see how far your mind goes with it. If you pray, let the question turn into thanks for the thing in front of you.

wordCard.voice: Dei Filius. The First Vatican Council's document teaching that faith and reason come from one God and can never truly contradict each other. Today's word.
